decision_basis: The canonical command invokes the production preprocessing, performance, permutation-plus-bootstrap Monte Carlo, sensitivity, and reporting engines in one ordered execution.
Every successful execution is atomically published to a unique results/runs/YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS directory and existing runs are never overwritten.
Versioned dataset, performance, and artifact schemas fail closed before run publication.
Thirty-five validation tests pass in both the project environment and a newly created temporary environment installed only from requirements-dev.txt.
The validated canonical run contains 323 accepted rows, 322 closed trades, 160000 Monte Carlo paths, 21 declared artifacts, and one manifest with zero hash mismatches.
Pine and all eight raw CSV hashes remained unchanged; shared legacy artifact hashes also remained unchanged.

Trade logs remain incomplete and non-comparable across timeframes; controlled HTF and entry-score outcomes, full cost/fill provenance, OOS/walk-forward evidence, and runtime TradingView equivalence remain absent.
remaining_limitations: Incomplete and cumulatively appended TradingView exports.
Small, heterogeneous, and period-incomparable timeframe samples.
Initial-capital provenance conflict between metadata/export and Pine declaration.
Incomplete commission, slippage, spread, fill, feed, timezone, and date-range provenance.
No controlled HTF Bias Timeframe or Minimum Entry Score experiment grid.
No preregistered OOS, walk-forward, cost-stress, cross-feed, or multiple-testing evidence.
No runtime TradingView compile and A/B backtest equivalence for the current Pine hash.
No full dependency lock with transitive hashes or CI evidence across operating systems.
